title: When the Protocol Falls Revisited
premise: Tamsin Reyes, a private security contractor shaped by a covert training program called the Protocol, receives a calendar invite from their dead handler, Mara Voss — and when they show up, the meeting is real, and so is the ambush. Hunted by the network that made them, Tamsin must decide whether loyalty to the people who forged them matters more than the truth of what that forging cost. With help from a rival contractor and Voss's posthumous evidence, Tamsin burns the Protocol's leadership from the inside, but the ending demands a price: Tamsin survives, exposed and unmoored, finally belonging to no one but themselves.
about_author: Tamsin Zhou is a former risk analyst who writes thrillers about institutions that love their people like equipment. They live between cities, keeping one bag packed out of habit.

chapters.title: The Invitation from a Dead Woman
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Between contracts, Tamsin maintains their polished cover story and go-bag until a calendar invite arrives from handler Mara Voss — killed three weeks ago. Compelled by old loyalty, Tamsin attends the coordinates. The emotional beat is unease sharpening into dread as the invite proves the network still speaks in Voss's voice.

chapters.title: Ambush at the Safehouse
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. The meeting is a trap: Protocol cleaners arrive to erase both the venue and Tamsin. Tamsin escapes through prepared escape routes only Voss could have planned, realizing she scheduled this death deliberately. The beat is betrayal curdling into a terrible suspicion: Voss meant for Tamsin to survive and see.

chapters.title: What the Training Bought
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV, with an interlude of recovered files. Flashbacks braid with present flight as Tamsin recalls how the Protocol recruited, isolated, and rewired them — belonging offered as a leash. The beat is grief: mourning the family that was also the cage, and choosing to keep running anyway.

chapters.title: The Rival
chapters.summary: Alternating POV with Nadia Okafor, a contractor from a competing firm who was also Protocol-trained and knows Tamsin's real name. Nadia offers alliance instead of a kill shot; neither trusts the other. The beat is wary kinship — two survivors recognizing the same scars, testing whether shared origin can become shared purpose.

chapters.title: Voss's Ledger
chapters.summary: Nadia decrypts Voss's dead-drop cache: names, payments, and proof the Protocol sells its graduates' loyalties to the highest bidder. Among the names is Tamsin's current client. The beat is cold clarity replacing nostalgia — the inheritance Voss left isn't sentiment, it's ammunition.

chapters.title: The Client Who Knew
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Guarding the client who secretly funded their own surveillance, Tamsin plays loyal while feeding the Protocol false telemetry. A near-exposure forces Tamsin to burn a safehouse and an identity. The beat is the thrill and terror of living the lie from the inside, loyalty and truth pulling apart.

chapters.title: Fracture
chapters.summary: Nadia's POV. The Protocol turns Nadia, threatening her brother, and she feeds Tamsin a poisoned route — then warns her at the last second, choosing truth over survival. The ambush fails; Nadia goes dark. The beat is heartbreak: the network's oldest weapon, leverage on love, breaking against a person's refusal.

chapters.title: Into the Vault
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Following Voss's final instructions, Tamsin infiltrates the Protocol's data vault during a leadership convocation, planting Voss's ledger where every operative will inherit it. Alarms, a confrontation with the director who trained them. The beat is the climax: Tamsin offering the director the same choice the Protocol never gave anyone.

chapters.title: Burn Notice
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. The ledger detonates across the network: operatives defect, clients flee, the director's inner circle turns. Tamsin fights free of the collapsing compound as Nadia resurfaces to cover the exit. The beat is catharsis and cost — the family burned down, its children scattered into open air.

chapters.title: Unpacked
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Weeks later, Tamsin testifies quietly, declines re-recruitment offers, and unpacks the go-bag for the first time in years. Meeting Nadia on neutral ground, they begin something unnamed and unowned. The beat is resolution: belonging rebuilt from choice, not training — inheritance kept, loyalty rewritten around truth.
